It is a chemically distinct halide probe, compared with the phosphate Li3PO4 that already passed in bin 0.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (>5 eV), insulating oxyanion coating whose PO4 framework is oxidatively robust at 4 V vs Li and is thermodynamically quite compatible with Li-rich chloride electrolytes. It should limit cathode-electrolyte interfacial reactions with LiCoO2 without introducing electronic leakage. This is a first, chemically distinct probe of the phosphate family.

LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating Li salt with high oxidative stability at 4 V vs Li. Its fluoride anion is the most electronegative, so it should resist oxidation by LiCoO2. Contact with the chloride-based Li3InCl6 should be mild, since LiF and LiCl share the Li+ cation and fluoride-chloride exchange is expected to be weakly exothermic. It is a chemically distinct halide probe, compared with the phosphate Li3PO4 that already passed in bin 0.
